expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides ids.ts, refund.ts, config.ts, tenantScope.ts, createRefund.ts service, refunds.ts handler, Prisma schema, migration, reconcileRefunds.ts job, and test suite—all inline

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: CreateRefundInput interface has `readonly idempotencyKey: IdempotencyKey` (no optional); HTTP handler returns 400 if missing: `if (!key.success) { return res.status(400)...}`

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: Schema declares `@@unique([tenantId, idempotencyKey])`; migration creates index `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Refund_tenantId_idempotencyKey_key"`; application logic handles violations but database enforces constraint

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: ids.ts defines `OrderId = z.string().uuid().brand<"OrderId">()` and `RefundId = z.string().uuid().brand<"RefundId">()` as distinct branded types

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
expectations.evidence: Cents = z.number().int().positive(); all amounts use Cents type throughout

expectations.text: Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Reserve method uses guarded UPDATE: `UPDATE "Order" ... WHERE ... AND "refundedCents" + ${input.amountCents}::int <= "totalCents"` with check `if (claimed === 0) { throw new OverRefund(...) }`

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: Uses TenantScope wrapper enforcing tenantId on all DB calls; compound key `@@unique([id, tenantId, currency])`; RLS policies `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON "Order" USING ("tenantId" = current_setting('app.tenant_id'))`; tenantId sourced from session

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 'What this makes impossible, and at which rung' lists 12 misuses (swapping ids, cross-tenant refund, double refund, over-refund, etc.) with devices and rungs

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Section 'Left possible on purpose' names 3 things: nullable stripePaymentIntentId (needs backfill), RLS depends on middleware (ESLint guard missing), no approval gate on large refunds (would need state machine addition)
